name: Kim Bong Carpentry Village
summary: Cross the Thu Bồn to the carpentry village opposite the old town, where wood has been worked since about the 16th century. Watch a carving demonstration, see the boatyards, and try a cut yourself. The carved houses of the old town are this village’s work. Give it a morning.
getThere: Cross the river to Cẩm Kim
heroCaption: A carver at work on a timber slab in Kim Bồng

notice.title: The village sells its own ticket
notice.body: Kim Bồng sells a visit ticket of its own, separate from the old-town building fee. Ask the price before you go in.

body: Kim Bồng sits on the south bank of the lower Thu Bồn, opposite the ancient town, in what was Cẩm Kim. The village dates to about the 16th century and still works wood in four lines: building timber, household wood, boatbuilding, and decorative carving. The old town’s carved houses, including Quân Thắng, are credited to its carpenters.
You can see the craft display, watch a demonstration, visit the boatyards, and try a cut. The village was listed as national intangible heritage on 21 November 2016.
Go in the morning. This is a working village across the river, not a hall on Trần Phú.

figures.caption: Carved wooden heads in the village
figures.alt: Three carved wooden faces with beards, made in Kim Bong carpentry village

gettingThere: The village is across the Thu Bồn from the old town.

legs.heading: From the old town
legs.body: Cross the river to Cẩm Kim.

admissionNote: A village visit ticket is sold; no price is published. Check on arrival. It is separate from the old-town building fee.
